submission.justification: R3 at 3 cm gives the best simulated separation of the radiators that I can credit with lifetime stability, 3.83 sigma. R2 separates better (4.66 sigma at 3 cm), but no document shows that it keeps its performance over the experiment's lifetime. It is a porous radiator with no hydrophobic treatment, and porous materials like this usually degrade when they take up moisture. The dry-nitrogen flush only covers operation, not storage or installation. R3 is the same kind of porous material with a hydrophobic treatment, which is the only lifetime protection mentioned. If the collaboration can show that R2 is stable, R2 at about 3 cm would give higher separation. I only simulated R3 at several thicknesses, and its separation peaks near 3 cm. R2 was simulated only at 3 cm, and R1 was not simulated. R1 had 2.9 sigma at 3 cm in the 2025 summary.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 peaks at 3 cm with 3.83 sigma. The other R3 results were 3.64 (2 cm), 3.72 (2.5 cm), 3.66 (4 cm), 3.40 (5 cm), 2.91 (6 cm) and 3.42 (1 cm). R2 is higher at 4.66 sigma at 3 cm, but its lifetime stability is unverified, so this is the best separation among the radiators I could accept.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates
Radiator keeps its performance over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: No document gives lifetime or aging data. R3 has a hydrophobic treatment, which suggests it resists moisture. R2 has no such treatment and is a risk. The dry N2 flush covers operation only.
